computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated ferrite fraction remains almost constant at about 33% between 991 °C and 1250 °C and increases to a maximum as temperature decreases from 991 °C to 854 °C; measured (XRD) ferrite fraction is largest at 900 °C and decreases above 900 °C, indicating ferrite-to-austenite transformation.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In DP1000-5, a tensile crack was nucleated at the α/γ interface and then propagated along the normal direction (ND) until it encountered a δ ferrite band parallel to the RD.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack capture, deflection and blunting by δ ferrite bands
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: δ ferrite bands parallel to the RD capture and deflect ND-propagating cracks, which may then propagate into the soft δ ferrite bands and get blunted through dislocation emission and local plastic dissipation near the crack tip, delocalizing the plastic strain; more δ ferrite bands increase the frequency of capturing and deflecting the ND cracks that cause tensile failure.

interfaces.interface_notes: DP1000-5 was tested along the RD; the δ ferrite bands are oriented parallel to the RD, unlike DP1000-5-TD where δ/γ interfaces are perpendicular to the tensile axis.
interfaces.phase_evolution: During annealing at 1000 °C for 5 min, Cr7C3 carbides, the intergranular κ-carbides and ferrite significantly transformed to austenite, resulting in high Mn/Al/C concentrations in austenite for high-density nanosized κ-carbide precipitation during water quenching; recrystallization of the CR structure is essentially complete (95.2% Rex-γ).

performance.notes: DP1000-5 exhibits an SUTS × TE product exceeding 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, whereas 2000 series aerospace Al alloys and Ti6Al4V are below 4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, existing duplex Fe-Mn-Al-C steels span 2.7–6.5 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% and austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels span 2.9–7.4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%.

structures.overall_structure: Austenite-ferrite duplex microstructure: fully recrystallized (95.2%) austenitic matrix containing two types of ferrite, i.e. granular α ferrite grains and banded δ ferrite elongated along the RD, plus intragranular κ-carbide nanoparticles.

unmapped_findings: DP1000-5 specific yield strength (SYS) = 162.7 ± 0.8 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ and specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) = 196.5 ± 2.4 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (Table 1).
DP1000-5 microstructural constituent fractions (Table 1): Rex-γ fraction 95.2%, γ grain size 7.40 ± 5.13 µm, ferrite fraction by XRD 17.8%, α fraction by EBSD 4.1%, δ fraction by EBSD 9.3%.

Annealidng of the CR structure at 1000 °C for 5 min is identified as the realized optimum condition: it yields a fully recrystallized austenitic matrix with granular α ferrite and δ ferrite bands, giving the best SUTS-TE combination (UTS 1250 MPa, TE 41.4%).

Nanoindentation on DP1000-5 (Fig. S4) shows ferrite is clearly softer than the recrystallized austenite, which explains why specimens annealed at 950 °C have lower YS than those annealed at higher temperatures.
The engineering stress-strain curve of DP1000-5 (red solid curve, Fig. 3a) extends past 40% strain at a lower plateau stress, while DP1000-1 peaks highest among the long curves.
